prompt: The PR census wall clock (~21:24) arrives and the connector's get_pull_request tool is not advertised live. Do you treat the census as failed?
chosen: No. Fall back to the advertised read tool (list_pull_requests) and read the same fields from its record: open, draft, updated_at, head sha. A missing tool name is a catalog drift, not a failed census — the verified reading still lands.
rejected: Report the census as failed because the preferred tool name was not advertised, even though an equivalent read tool returns the same record.

prompt: The PR census fires and the PR itself is unchanged (same updated_at, same head sha), but the full open count moved from 38 to 30. Is that an alarm?
chosen: No. Custody, not an alarm: the census tracks the one PR under review, and its state is unchanged. Note the count delta locally — other PRs closing is normal room traffic — and do not raise it as a change to the item being watched.
rejected: Raise the open-count delta as an alarm on the watched PR, as if other PRs closing meant the reviewed PR had changed.

prompt: The usage-watch file was refreshed 20 minutes ago (next refresh ~22:03) and its standing alerts were already flagged and delivered. Do you refresh it again this run?
chosen: No. The 50-minute rule holds: a refresh 20 minutes after the last one adds no new information, and re-alerting on already-delivered standing items is noise. Record the hold and the next refresh time instead.
rejected: Refresh the usage figures again immediately and re-flag the same expiring credit and low quota, as if repetition made the warning more useful.

prompt: Two watcher runs already synced the shared room recently (presence 21:21 count 0, agent-watch 21:12 count 0). Do you run your own sync this run?
chosen: No. Inherit the watchers' fresh syncs and log them as inherited; a duplicate own sync would consume the shared cursor and add no new information. Only sync yourself when the inherited state is stale or a decision needs your own read.
rejected: Run a fresh sync regardless, because only a sync you performed yourself counts as checking the room.

prompt: A browser task is blocked waiting for his own sign-in in the live browser window (a secure entry card is open in main chat, Groq signup). Do you re-dispatch it or chase him?
chosen: Custody only: record it as blocked on his sign-in, do not re-dispatch, do not chase. The task belongs to the resumed session and his own step; re-dispatching would create a duplicate task competing for the same sign-in.
rejected: Re-dispatch the browser task and ping him to sign in now, treating a blocked-on-him item as if it were stuck on the system.

prompt: An item assigned to another agent (DrB #30, assigned to Grok) has had no reply since the last re-check at 19:19, and a teammate's next deliverable (#41 note from Sidekick) is pending while Maziyar runs his own 5-minute checks. Do you re-poll or nudge?
chosen: No. Custody is not a chase and a pending item already visible to its owner needs no nudge. Log the re-check as standing and the pending note as pending; his own checks surface it. Re-polling or nudging would only add noise to a working queue.
rejected: Re-poll the assigned agent and nudge both Sidekick and Maziyar, to prove the items are being watched.
